# The Slingshot

> The Slingshot is a free, open-source simulation of founding and running an AI startup, built for teaching entrepreneurial strategy in nascent industries, technology venturing, innovation management and technology commercialisation. It runs in the browser with nothing to install; a game takes twenty-five to forty minutes. It was created by Ammon Salter (Warwick Business School), with Stefano Baruffaldi (Politecnico di Milano) and Federico Bignone (Warwick Business School), out of the ESRC-funded research project "Profiting from Science" (ES/X003949/1).

Players act as the first-time chief executive of an AI startup in the United Kingdom, running the venture quarter by quarter across four years (sixteen quarters) and racing rival firms to three milestones before money or time runs out. The game builds on the attention-based view of the firm (Ocasio, 1997), with attention the scarce resource allocated between competing goals each quarter. It covers team building, fundraising (dilution, term sheets, venture capital and non-dilutive grants), market selection using the Where to Play framework (Gruber and Tal, 2017), stakeholder management and university-industry interaction: engaging the science base, deciding whether to publish or protect, and building university partnerships. Its eight sectors are grounded in the real UK AI ecosystem, with mini-cases inspired by firms such as Isomorphic Labs, Wayve, Synthesia, Darktrace, Lendable, Sylvera, Robin AI and Multiverse.

Three modes serve different cohorts: Seed (forgiving, for first-time players and introductory undergraduate teaching), Core (the standard game, with live competitive benchmarking, suited to postgraduate and executive teaching) and Extreme (for advanced cohorts studying decision-making under severe uncertainty). Failure and replay are part of the design: most students fail their first run, runs are short enough to play again, and players play against themselves, chasing a higher valuation with a different firm set-up each time. Three mini-games (conference booth, investor pitch, demo day) sit inside the simulation. Version 2 (June 2026) added Seed mode, competitive play with zero-cost in-class tournaments (no registration, no personal data), the Market Opportunity Navigator, the Token Spend mechanic and a venture that regenerates between milestones. Since launch in January 2026 it has been played by more than 1,900 people in 60 countries (as of July 2026). It is free, with no accounts and no student data collected. A free educator pack (an Educator's Companion covering mechanics and teaching notes, a Player's Companion, a ready-to-teach slide deck, ideas for reflective assessment, eight venture-matched mini-cases of real UK AI startups, and two AI assistants for players and educators) is available on request from ammon.salter@wbs.ac.uk.

## Play

- [Play The Slingshot](https://slingshotsim.org/play): the game itself, in the browser, free.

## For educators

- [For Educators](https://slingshotsim.org/educators.html): who the game is for, learning objectives, modes, cohort guidance and how to request the free educator pack.
- [How to Play](https://slingshotsim.org/how-to-play.html): rules and systems overview.
- [UK AI Ecosystem](https://slingshotsim.org/uk-ecosystem.html): the real-world grounding of the game's sectors, funders and milestones.

## Background

- [About](https://slingshotsim.org/about.html): the research project behind the game, who built it, and how.
- [Source code](https://github.com/ammonsalter-del/The-Slingshot-Simulation): the open-source repository.
